```{r setup}
# The working directory is this folder, shared layer is two levels up
source("../../common/setup.R")

source("R/metrics.R")
source("R/preflight.R")

con <- connect_athena()

accent <- "#115740"
# Forest mixed 45% with white, for the informational topic bars
accent_light <- "#7CA396"

# A failed check adds a banner. See R/preflight.R.
preflight <- run_preflight_safety_check(con, today = Sys.Date())
write_preflight_status(preflight)

# The two sources are current to different days
data_through <- call_centre_data_through(con)
snapshot_date <- psom_snapshot_date(con)

psom_through <- snapshot_date - 1L

# How far back every weekly chart runs
chart_from <- seq(as.Date(format(max(data_through, psom_through), "%Y-%m-01")),
                  by = "-2 months", length.out = 2)[2]

# For a card title, where the exact dates are on the axis below it.
chart_span_label <- "last three months"

# "Aug 8"
format_short_date <- function(d) {
  d <- as.Date(d)
  paste0(format(d, "%b"), " ", as.integer(format(d, "%d")))
}

# "August 8", not "August 08"
format_long_date <- function(d) {
  d <- as.Date(d)
  paste0(format(d, "%B"), " ", as.integer(format(d, "%d")))
}

window_label <- glue("last {tolower(fmt_count(summary_window_weeks, 'week'))}")
prior_window_label <- "vs previous"

page_header <- "page-header.html"

write_preflight_banner(preflight, page_header)

cat(
  c(
    '<div class="page-strip">',
    glue("  <p><strong>Call centre data through {format_long_date(data_through)}, ",
         "PSOM board as of {format_long_date(psom_through)}.",
         "</strong> Internal to Enterprise Digital Credentials, not for public ",
         "consumption.</p>"),
    "</div>"
  ),
  file = page_header, sep = "\n", append = TRUE
)

# Each figure names the date of the source behind it.
brand_figure <- function(p, height = 0.09, date = data_through) {
  add_cds_logo(
    add_watermark(p, report_name = "CanadaLogin Support", date = date),
    height = height
  )
}

# A bar spans its seven days and its tick sits at the end of that span, so the
# two move together.
week_offset <- 3.5
week_tick_offset <- 7L

week_axis <- function(weeks, limits = NULL, max_labels = 14L,
                      expand = waiver()) {
  weeks <- sort(unique(weeks))
  # Every other week past max_labels, counted back so the newest keeps its.
  step <- if (length(weeks) > max_labels) 2L else 1L
  labelled <- rev(weeks[seq(length(weeks), 1L, by = -step)])
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = labelled + week_tick_offset,
    labels = format(labelled + 6L, "%b %d"),
    limits = limits,
    expand = expand
  )
}

# Goes with week_axis(), which labels a bar with the last day it covers.
week_axis_title <- "Week ending"

table_options <- function(table) {
  tab_options(
    table,
    table.width = pct(100),
    table.font.size = px(14),
    data_row.padding = px(4),
    table.border.top.style = "none"
  )
}
```

# Overview

## Row {height="330px"}

::: {.card title="About this dashboard"}

This dashboard reports the **support the CanadaLogin team provides**.
It is internal to Enterprise Digital Credentials and the link is unlisted, so
it isn't visible to the general public. It's for *your* information. For
anything that leaves EDCP, please reach out to the
[Data and Research team](https://gcdigital.slack.com/archives/C0A6S9F7KV4). We
are happy to provide you with a bespoke calculation or the underlying data.

**A red banner at the top of the page means a check failed at render time.** Do
not quote anything until it clears. If you don't see a red banner (it's hard to
miss), then you can assume that all of the data quality checks passed.

The definitions come from the
[metrics cookbook](https://cds-snc.github.io/canadalogin-metrics-cookbook/cookbook/call_centre.html),
which is the source of truth. This page is republished in place every week.

:::

## Row

::: {.card title="About the call centre"}

The **Call centre** page counts calls from members of the public to the
CanadaLogin support line. The call centre sends a weekly report covering
Sunday to Saturday, a few days after the week ends, so the newest week here is
usually last week's. Each call's reason is recorded as a *topic*. One call may
cover several topics, and some calls have no topic recorded at all.

The **Partner support** page counts tickets on the Partner Success and
Operations (PSOM) Jira board, where departments integrating a service with
CanadaLogin ask for help. This includes things like onboarding requests, environment
access, and escalations to product teams. It is not where members of the public go.

Volumes are small: a few dozen calls or a couple of tickets a week. A change
of a few calls turns into a large percentage, so trust the counts before the
percentages. Every comparison is the last four reported weeks against the four
before them.

:::

# Call centre

```{r calls-summary}
#| include: false

weeks <- call_weeks(con)
topics <- call_topics(con)

current <- recent_weeks(weeks, data_through)
prior <- prior_weeks(weeks, data_through)

calls_now <- sum(current$calls)
calls_prior <- sum(prior$calls)
calls_delta <- fmt_delta(relative_change(calls_now, calls_prior))

wait_now <- weighted_weekly(current, "avg_delay_seconds")
abandoned_now <- sum(current$calls_abandoned)
length_now <- weighted_weekly(current, "avg_call_length_seconds")

window_weeks_label <- glue(
  "{format_short_date(min(current$week))} to {format_short_date(max(current$week_end))}"
)

# The charts run on the reported weeks ending inside the charted span.
charted <- weeks |> filter(week_end >= chart_from)
```

```{r calls-chart}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.1
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Bar chart of calls to the CanadaLogin support line per week, one bar per
#|   reported week, excluding test calls.

p <- ggplot(charted, aes(week + week_offset, calls)) +
  geom_col(width = 7, fill = accent, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(aes(label = calls), vjust = -0.5, size = 3, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = pretty_breaks(5),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  week_axis(charted$week) +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = week_axis_title, y = "Calls",
       subtitle = "Calls accepted by the support line each week, excluding test calls.")

brand_figure(p)
```

## Row {height="420px"}

::: {.card title="`r glue('Why users called ({window_label})')`"}

```{r topics-chart}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Two horizontal bar charts side by side, sharing a calls axis: informational
#|   topics on the left, troubleshooting topics on the right. Each shows up to five
#|   groups of calls over the last four weeks by what they were about, sorted from
#|   most to least common, each bar labelled with its count of calls and its share
#|   of all calls in the window.

window_topics <- topics_in_weeks(topics, current)

topic_types <- c("Informational", "Troubleshooting")
panel_slots <- 5L

# distinct() so a call recorded against two topics in one category counts once
by_category <- window_topics |>
  distinct(call_no, category) |>
  count(category, name = "calls") |>
  # Keep every named category on the axis so the chart always has the same rows
  complete(category = factor(topic_category_levels, levels = topic_category_levels),
           fill = list(calls = 0L)) |>
  filter(category != "Other" | calls > 0) |>
  mutate(category = as.character(category),
         type = factor(topic_category_type(category), levels = topic_types)) |>
  group_by(type) |>
  # A tie at fifth place is broken alphabetically, so a panel never shows six
  arrange(desc(calls), category, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = panel_slots) |>
  ungroup()

# Each panel has five slots, so a bar is the same thickness in both however many
# categories a type has. A slot with no category is a blank row, named with a
# distinct run of spaces so the rows stay apart on the axis.
empty_slots <- by_category |>
  count(type, name = "used", .drop = FALSE) |>
  mutate(missing = panel_slots - used) |>
  filter(missing > 0) |>
  tidyr::uncount(missing, .id = "slot") |>
  mutate(category = strrep(" ", as.integer(type) * panel_slots + slot),
         calls = NA_integer_) |>
  select(type, category, calls)

by_category <- bind_rows(by_category, empty_slots) |>
  # Blank rows first, so they sit at the foot of the panel
  arrange(!is.na(calls), calls, desc(category)) |>
  mutate(category = factor(category, levels = category))

bars <- filter(by_category, !is.na(calls))

# Calls the report counted that the topic dump has no reason
calls_without_topic <- calls_now - n_distinct(window_topics$call_no)

p <- ggplot(by_category, aes(calls, category)) +
  geom_blank() +
  geom_col(data = bars, aes(fill = type), width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = bars,
            aes(label = paste0(calls, " (", round(100 * calls / calls_now), "%)")),
            hjust = -0.2, size = 3.2, colour = "grey30") +
  # Fixed x so the two panels compare directly
  facet_wrap(~type, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = pretty_breaks(4),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Troubleshooting = accent,
                               Informational = accent_light)) +
  theme_cds() +
  # Every bar is labelled, and a tick on a blank slot would point at nothing
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = "Calls", y = NULL,
       subtitle = glue("Calls by what they were about, {window_weeks_label}, ",
                       "from the topics the call centre recorded."))

brand_figure(p)
```

::: {.figure-note}
Each bar counts **calls**, not topic records. One call may have many topics, one or 
none. Because of that, the percentages do not necessarily add to 100%.
:::

:::

## Row

::: {.card title="`r glue('Call metrics ({window_label})')`"}

```{r metrics-table}
# One row per metric for cols_nanoplot()
# nolint start: line_length_linter. Keep aligned table columns.
call_metrics <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label,                           ~column,                   ~unit,      ~good,  ~agg,
  "Calls, excluding test calls",    "calls",                   "count",    NA,     "mean",
  "Calls accepted",                 "calls_accepted",          "count",    NA,     "mean",
  "Calls abandoned",                "calls_abandoned",         "count",    "down", "mean",
  "Escalations to PSO (callbacks)", "callbacks",               "count",    "down", "mean",
  "Answered within 60 s",           "pct_answered_within_60s", "percent",  "up",   "weighted",
  "Avg. call wait (m:s)",           "avg_delay_seconds",        "duration", "down", "weighted",
  "Avg. call length (m:s)",         "avg_call_length_seconds",  "duration", NA,     "weighted"
)
# nolint end

# One column holds every unit, so a value is formatted before it gets there and
# the row label carries the unit.
fmt_metric <- function(x, unit) {
  switch(unit,
    count = format(round(x, 1), big.mark = ","),
    percent = sprintf("%.0f%%", x * 100),
    duration = fmt_minutes(x)
  )
}

# The summary window, oldest first, so a row reads left to right into its trend.
window_weeks <- charted |>
  slice_max(week_end, n = summary_window_weeks) |>
  arrange(week_end)

week_labels <- format_short_date(window_weeks$week_end)
newest <- nrow(window_weeks)

# One formatted string per metric per week: metrics down the rows, weeks across.
cells <- t(mapply(\(col, unit) fmt_metric(window_weeks[[col]], unit),
                  call_metrics$column, call_metrics$unit))
colnames(cells) <- week_labels

arrows <- c(up = "\u25b2", down = "\u25bc", flat = "\u2013")

# Sometimes up is good and sometimes up is bad. We use "good"/"bad" to be explicit
verdict_colours <- c(good = "#008B45",
                     bad = colors$brand[["red"]],
                     none = "#5C6670")
verdict_weights <- c(good = "700", bad = "700", none = "400")

direction <- purrr::map_chr(call_metrics$column, \(col) {
  delta_direction(relative_change(window_weeks[[col]][newest],
                                  window_weeks[[col]][newest - 1L]))
})

verdict <- purrr::map2_chr(direction, call_metrics$good, \(moved, good) {
  if (moved == "flat" || is.na(good)) "none" else if (moved == good) "good" else "bad"
})

# Only the newest week carries an arrow; the earlier columns are the record.
cells[, newest] <- paste0(
  cells[, newest],
  ' <span style="color: ', verdict_colours[verdict],
  "; font-weight: ", verdict_weights[verdict], '">', arrows[direction], "</span>"
)

# Counts just use a regular average, not weighted
averages <- purrr::pmap_chr(
  list(call_metrics$column, call_metrics$unit, call_metrics$agg),
  \(col, unit, agg) {
    fmt_metric(
      if (agg == "weighted") {
        weighted_weekly(window_weeks, col)
      } else {
        mean(window_weeks[[col]])
      },
      unit
    )
  }
)

series <- charted |>
  arrange(week_end) |>
  transmute(week = format(week_end, "w%m%d"), across(all_of(call_metrics$column))) |>
  pivot_longer(-week, names_to = "column") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = week, values_from = value)

dplyr::bind_cols(call_metrics["label"], tibble::tibble(average = averages),
                 as.data.frame(cells)) |>
  mutate(column = call_metrics$column) |>
  left_join(series, by = "column") |>
  select(-column) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = all_of(week_labels[newest])) |>
  cols_nanoplot(
    columns = -c(label, average, all_of(week_labels)),
    plot_type = "bar",
    # Bars run from zero, so a metric that only moves between four and five
    # draws even bars rather than a sawtooth.
    expand_y = 0,
    new_col_name = "trend",
    new_col_label = glue("Trend, {chart_span_label}"),
    options = nanoplot_options(
      data_bar_fill_color = accent,
      data_bar_stroke_color = accent
    )
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    label = "",
    average = html(glue("{fmt_count(summary_window_weeks)}-week<br>average"))
  ) |>
  cols_align("right", columns = c(average, all_of(week_labels))) |>
  cols_align("center", columns = trend) |>
  # Ruled off, or a column of averages sitting in front of four date headings
  # reads as another week.
  tab_style(
    cell_borders(sides = "right", color = "#DFE2E5", weight = px(1)),
    list(cells_body(columns = average), cells_column_labels(columns = average))
  ) |>
  cols_width(label ~ pct(24), trend ~ pct(28), everything() ~ pct(9.6)) |>
  table_options()
```

::: {.figure-note}

The color of the arrow indications whether the movement is positive or negative, 
independent of the direction. Some metrics do not an inherent value to their movement,
so they are coloured grey.

*Accepted* is every call that reached the queue, answered or abandoned. *Calls* is 
accepted minus test calls. Averages are the call centre's own weekly figures.

:::

:::

# Partner support

```{r psom-summary}
#| include: false

board <- psom_board(psom_snapshots(con))

opened_now <- nrow(created_in_window(board, psom_through))
opened_prior <- nrow(created_in_window(board, psom_through - summary_window_days))
opened_delta <- fmt_delta(relative_change(opened_now, opened_prior))

closed_now <- nrow(closed_in_window(board, psom_through))
closed_prior <- nrow(closed_in_window(board, psom_through - summary_window_days))
closed_delta <- fmt_delta(relative_change(closed_now, closed_prior))

# Median, not mean: the tail is long enough that a few slow tickets would set it.
ages <- psom_ages(board, psom_through)
median_age <- fmt_days(median(ages$age))

# Calendar months, the current one to date. Tickets archived before the first
# snapshot were never recorded, so a month before it would read short.
psom_recorded_from <- min(psom_snapshots(con)$snapshot)
monthly <- psom_monthly(board, psom_months_from(psom_through), psom_through)

# "Aug", with the year under the first month and every January; the current
# month says how far it runs.
month_label <- function(month, month_end, partial) {
  last_day <- as.integer(format(month_end, "%d"))
  label <- if_else(partial, as.character(glue("{format(month, '%b')} 1-{last_day}")),
                   format(month, "%b"))
  show_year <- seq_along(month) == 1L | format(month, "%m") == "01"
  if_else(show_year, paste0(label, "\n", format(month, "%Y")), label)
}

# Panel order. Opened and closed are flows; the queue is the level they leave.
panels <- c(opened = "Tickets opened", closed = "Tickets completed",
            open = "Tickets awaiting handling")
panel_fill <- setNames(c(accent, accent_light, "#5C6670"), panels)

charted_psom <- monthly |>
  mutate(label = factor(month_label(month, month_end, partial),
                        levels = month_label(month, month_end, partial))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(opened, closed, open), names_to = "measure",
               values_to = "tickets") |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panels[measure], levels = panels))

psom_queue_caveats <- paste0(
  if (any(monthly$partial)) {
    glue(" {format(psom_through, '%B')} runs only to ",
         "{format_long_date(psom_through)}, so its counts are partial.")
  } else {
    ""
  },
  if (psom_recorded_from > min(monthly$month)) {
    glue(" The board was first recorded on {format_long_date(psom_recorded_from)}, ",
         "so tickets opened and archived before then are missing.")
  } else {
    ""
  }
)

# Counts are whole tickets, so a half-ticket break would be nonsense.
whole_breaks <- function(x) {
  breaks <- pretty_breaks(4)(x)
  breaks[breaks == floor(breaks)]
}

# SLA clocks, each counted in the complete week it stopped
sla_week_starts <- sla_weeks(psom_through)
sla_last <- psom_sla_last(psom_sla_snapshots(con))
outcomes <- sla_outcomes(sla_last, max(sla_week_starts) + 6L) |>
  filter(stopped_week %in% sla_week_starts)
sla_by_week <- sla_weekly(outcomes, sla_week_starts)

# Who handled the tickets opened in the window, and what they were about
handled <- psom_handled_by(psom_snapshots(con), psom_through)
topics <- board |>
  created_in_window(psom_through) |>
  filter(status != "Canceled") |>
  psom_topic_counts()
```

## Row

::: {.card title="Service levels by week"}

```{r sla-scorecard}
cell_headline <- function(x) {
  glue("<div style='font-size:20px;font-weight:700;line-height:1.1'>{x}</div>")
}
cell_line <- function(x) glue("<div style='font-size:12px'>{x}</div>")
empty_cell <- "<div style='color:#767676'>-</div>"

# Share within target, then the count behind it, then the median time
sla_cell <- function(share, met, stopped, median_hours) {
  if_else(
    stopped == 0, empty_cell,
    paste0(cell_headline(fmt_pct(share)),
           cell_line(glue("{met} of {stopped} within target")),
           cell_line(glue("median {fmt_work_time(median_hours)}")))
  )
}

# Pooled over the weeks shown, not a median of weekly medians
sla_pooled <- outcomes |>
  group_by(sla) |>
  sla_tally() |>
  right_join(tibble(sla = names(sla_clocks)), by = "sla") |>
  mutate(across(c(met, stopped), \(x) coalesce(x, 0L)))

week_cols <- as.character(sla_week_starts)
scorecard <- bind_rows(mutate(sla_by_week, col = as.character(week)),
                       mutate(sla_pooled, col = "all")) |>
  mutate(cell = sla_cell(share, met, stopped, median_hours)) |>
  select(sla, col, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = cell) |>
  mutate(
    target = purrr::map_chr(sla, \(s) sla_target_label(sla_last, s)),
    name = glue("<b>{sla_clocks[sla]}</b><br>",
                "<span style='font-size:12px;color:#555'>{target}</span>"),
    sla = factor(sla, levels = names(sla_clocks))
  ) |>
  arrange(sla) |>
  select(name, all_of(week_cols), all)

# Quarto stripes every table; the pooled column's shading does that job here
scorecard |>
  gt(id = "sla-scorecard") |>
  opt_css(paste("#sla-scorecard table > tbody > tr > *",
                "{ --bs-table-bg-type: transparent; }")) |>
  fmt_passthrough(columns = everything(), escape = FALSE) |>
  cols_label(.list = c(
    list(name = "", all = md(glue("**All {length(sla_week_starts)} weeks**"))),
    setNames(as.list(format_short_date(sla_week_starts + 6L)), week_cols)
  )) |>
  cols_align("center", columns = -name) |>
  cols_align("left", columns = name) |>
  tab_spanner("Week ending", columns = all_of(week_cols)) |>
  tab_style(cell_fill("#EEF0F2"), cells_body(columns = all)) |>
  tab_style(cell_borders(sides = "bottom", color = "#D0D4D8", weight = px(1)),
            cells_body()) |>
  table_options()
```

::: {.figure-note}
- **Time to first response:** how long a partner waits for PSO's first reply.
- **PSO handling:** PSO's time on a ticket. The clock pauses while a ticket is escalated
  to another team.
- **Auth product team handling:** the time a ticket spends escalated to the Auth product
  team.
- **Time to done:** how long the whole ticket takes, from opened to done. The clock keeps
  running while a ticket is escalated.

Clocks count working hours only, 9 to 5 on weekdays, and pause while a ticket waits for
the partner. A ticket counts in the week its clock stopped, as in Jira's SLA success rate
report. Targets changed on October 15, 2026, but not retroactively: earlier tickets are
still judged on the old ones.
:::

:::

## Row {height="auto"}

::: {.card title="`r glue('What tickets were about ({window_label})')`"}

```{r psom-topics}
# A bar as wide as the share
share_bar <- function(share, fill = accent) {
  glue("<div style='background:{fill};width:{round(100 * share)}%;height:14px'></div>")
}

# Shares are of all tickets opened, not of the section
topic_share <- function(rows) {
  mutate(rows, share = tickets / nrow(handled), bar = share_bar(share))
}

# Each section's total over its topics, then its topics, most common first;
# no topic last, as a section on its own
section_rows <- topics |>
  summarise(tickets = sum(tickets), .by = section) |>
  arrange(section == "No topic given", desc(tickets), section) |>
  mutate(label = section, level = "section", order = 0L)
topic_rows <- topics |>
  filter(section != "No topic given") |>
  arrange(desc(tickets), topic) |>
  mutate(label = topic, level = "topic", order = row_number())
total_row <- tibble(label = "All tickets", tickets = nrow(handled),
                    level = "total")

bind_rows(section_rows, topic_rows) |>
  mutate(section = factor(section, levels = section_rows$section)) |>
  arrange(section, order) |>
  bind_rows(total_row) |>
  topic_share() |>
  mutate(bar = if_else(level == "total", "", bar)) |>
  select(label, tickets, share, bar, level) |>
  gt(id = "psom-topics") |>
  opt_css(paste("#psom-topics table > tbody > tr > *",
                "{ --bs-table-bg-type: transparent; }")) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = share, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_passthrough(columns = bar, escape = FALSE) |>
  cols_hide(level) |>
  cols_label(label = "", tickets = "Tickets", share = "Share", bar = "") |>
  cols_align("left", columns = c(label, bar)) |>
  cols_align("right", columns = c(tickets, share)) |>
  cols_width(bar ~ pct(40)) |>
  tab_style(list(cell_text(weight = "bold"), cell_fill("#EEF0F2")),
            cells_body(rows = level == "section")) |>
  tab_style(cell_text(indent = px(16)),
            cells_body(columns = label, rows = level == "topic")) |>
  tab_style(list(cell_text(weight = "bold"),
                 cell_borders(sides = "top", color = "#1B1B1B", weight = px(2))),
            cells_body(rows = level == "total")) |>
  table_options()
```

::: {.figure-note}
The topic picked on the support form, under its section of the form, as a share of all
tickets opened. A ticket with two topics counts under both, so the shares can add to more
than 100%.
:::

:::

::: {.card title="`r glue('Who handled tickets ({window_label})')`"}

```{r psom-handled-by}
handled_fill <- setNames(c(accent, accent_light, "#5C6670"),
                         psom_handled_by_levels)

handled |>
  count(handled_by, .drop = FALSE, name = "tickets") |>
  mutate(share = tickets / sum(tickets),
         bar = share_bar(share, handled_fill[as.character(handled_by)])) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_percent(columns = share, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_passthrough(columns = bar, escape = FALSE) |>
  cols_label(handled_by = "", tickets = "Tickets", share = "Share", bar = "") |>
  cols_align("left", columns = c(handled_by, bar)) |>
  cols_align("right", columns = c(tickets, share)) |>
  cols_width(bar ~ pct(40)) |>
  table_options()
```

::: {.figure-note}
`r fmt_count(nrow(handled), "ticket")` opened in the last four weeks, cancelled ones left
out, by the first team each was escalated to. A ticket never escalated counts as PSO
alone, even one still open that may be escalated later.
:::

```{r psom-flow-chart}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Three stacked bar charts sharing a monthly axis, each in its own colour:
#|   tickets opened per calendar month, tickets completed per month, and
#|   tickets awaiting handling at the end of each month. The axis covers up to

p <- ggplot(charted_psom, aes(label, tickets, fill = panel)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(tickets > 0, tickets, "")), vjust = -0.7,
            size = 2.6, colour = "grey30") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", strip.position = "top",
```

## Row {height="auto"}

::: {.card title="Open tickets"}

```{r sla-open}
open_tickets <- psom_open(psom_latest(con))
open_clocks <- sla_open_clocks(psom_sla_snapshots(con), open_tickets$key)

# Bold red past target, so it does not rest on colour alone
past_target_style <- glue("color:{colors$brand[['red']]};font-weight:700")

if (nrow(open_tickets) == 0) {
  cat("No tickets are open.")
} else {
  # Working time so far; a clock not yet started is a dash
  clock_cells <- open_clocks |>
    mutate(
      cell = case_when(
        is.na(breached) ~ "-",
        breached ~ glue("<span style='{past_target_style}'>",
                        "{fmt_work_time(elapsed_hours)}</span>"),
        .default = fmt_work_time(elapsed_hours)
      ),
      sla = factor(sla, levels = names(sla_clocks))
    ) |>
    select(key, sla, cell) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = sla, values_from = cell, names_expand = TRUE,
                values_fill = "-")

  # "PSO handling" in bold over "Target: 40 working hours"
  clock_labels <- purrr::map(names(sla_clocks), \(s) {
    html(glue("<b>{sla_clocks[[s]]}</b><br><span style='font-weight:400'>",
              "{sla_target_label(sla_last, s)}</span>"))
  }) |>
    setNames(names(sla_clocks))

  open_tickets |>
    select(key, status, created) |>
    left_join(clock_cells, by = "key") |>
    mutate(across(all_of(names(sla_clocks)), \(x) coalesce(x, "-"))) |>
    arrange(psom_key_number(key)) |>
    mutate(
      ticket = glue("<a href='{psom_ticket_url(key)}'>{key}</a>"),
      opened = format_short_date(created)
    ) |>
    select(ticket, status, opened, all_of(names(sla_clocks))) |>
    gt() |>
    fmt_passthrough(columns = c(ticket, all_of(names(sla_clocks))), escape = FALSE) |>
    cols_label(.list = c(list(ticket = "Ticket", status = "Status", opened = "Opened"),
                         clock_labels)) |>
    tab_spanner("Working time so far", columns = all_of(names(sla_clocks))) |>
    cols_align("left") |>
    table_options() |>
    # Smaller and tighter than the other tables: a reference list, not a headline
    tab_options(table.font.size = px(12), column_labels.font.size = px(12),
                data_row.padding = px(2), column_labels.padding = px(2),
                table.font.color = "#555555")
}

# The download is embedded in the page: publishing copies only the HTML file.
export_from <- chart_from
ticket_export <- psom_ticket_export(psom_snapshots(con), psom_sla_snapshots(con),
                                    export_from)
export_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
utils::write.csv(ticket_export, export_file, row.names = FALSE, na = "")
export_href <- paste0("data:text/csv;base64,", base64enc::base64encode(export_file))
export_name <- glue("psom-tickets-{psom_through}.csv")
```

::: {.figure-note}
[Download](`r export_href`){download="`r export_name`"} the last three months of tickets
as a CSV.
:::

# Support ratios

```{r ratios-summary}
#| include: false

# Step 1: how often a service's users sign in, across public applications
login_through <- max(app_logins(con)$date)
daily_share <- application_daily_share(
  app_logins(con), application_is_internal(con), login_through
)

# Steps 2 and 3: four reported weeks at a time, since escalation began
ratio_weeks <- weeks |> filter(week_end >= escalation_start)
weekly_rate <- call_rate(ratio_weeks, daily_active_users(con))
windows <- rolling_windows(ratio_weeks)
window_rates <- window_call_rate(weekly_rate, windows) |>
  left_join(
    # Not `topics`, which the Partner support page has taken over by now
    window_escalation_rate(call_topics(con), windows) |>
      select(window_end, dump_calls = calls, escalations, escalation_rate),
    by = "window_end"
  ) |>
  # Drawn at the centre of its last week, beside that week's own dot
  mutate(x = window_end - 6L + week_offset)

# Single weeks, for the grey dots under each four-week line
weekly_escalation <- window_escalation_rate(
  call_topics(con), rolling_windows(ratio_weeks, size = 1L)
)

# The charts run on the page's usual span, so old weeks age off. The diagram
# draws from the same four-week stretches the charts show.
ratio_charted <- ratio_weeks |> filter(week_end >= chart_from)
ratio_x <- range(ratio_charted$week) + week_offset
drawn <- window_rates |> filter(window_end >= chart_from)

# Every call in the stretches drawn, once, for the counts behind the rate
drawn_pooled <- window_escalation_rate(
  call_topics(con),
  tibble(window_start = min(drawn$window_start), window_end = max(drawn$window_end))
)

steps <- bind_rows(
  daily_share = quartiles(daily_share$daily_share),
  calls_per_100 = quartiles(drawn$calls_per_100),
  escalation_rate = quartiles(drawn$escalation_rate),
  .id = "step"
)
step <- split(steps, steps$step)

projection <- support_projection(daily_share$daily_share,
                                 drawn$calls_per_100,
                                 drawn$escalation_rate)
stage <- split(projection, projection$stage)

monthly_users_label <- fmt_rounded(projection_monthly_users, 1)

pct1 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
# calls_per_100 is already per cent of daily users, and keeps the public
# figure's two decimals
calls_pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f%%", x)

# "range: 6,400 to 9,400", worded the same in the diagram and the charts
fmt_range <- function(x, fmt) glue("range: {fmt(x$low)} to {fmt(x$high)}")

# Both ratio charts are drawn by this, so they read as a pair
ratio_chart <- function(rows, weekly, y, ratio, fmt, y_title,
                        y_labels = waiver()) {
  rows <- filter(rows, !is.na(.data[[y]]))
  weekly <- weekly |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[y]]), window_end >= chart_from) |>
    mutate(x = window_start + week_offset)

  p <- ggplot(rows, aes(x, .data[[y]])) +
    # The arrow's middle half and median, from the green points
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = ratio$low,
             ymax = ratio$high, fill = accent, alpha = 0.12) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = ratio$median, colour = accent, linetype = "dashed",
               linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(data = weekly, colour = "grey60", size = 2.2) +
    geom_line(colour = accent, linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(colour = accent, size = 1.6) +
    # In the head room below the logo, worded as on the arrow: beside the
    # line, the label can cross a point
    annotate("text", x = max(rows$x), y = Inf, vjust = 2.2, hjust = 0.85,
             label = glue("Median {fmt(ratio$median)}\n",
                          fmt_range(ratio, fmt)),
             colour = accent, fontface = "bold", size = 3.2, lineheight = 0.9) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = y_labels, breaks = pretty_breaks(5),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.45))) +
    # Not a scale limit, which would silently drop the line falling below it
    expand_limits(x = ratio_x, y = 0) +
    # An extra week of slack so we don't accidentally truncate labels
    week_axis(ratio_charted$week, max_labels = 9L,
              expand = expansion(add = c(2, 7))) +
    theme_cds() +
    # Narrow tick labels otherwise run into the title
    theme(axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8))) +
    labs(x = week_axis_title, y = y_title,
         subtitle = paste0("Grey: each week. Green: the rate over four weeks.\n",
                           "Band and dashed line: their middle half and median."))
  brand_figure(p, height = 0.11)
}
```

## Row {height="auto"}

::: {.card title="About support ratios"}

A **support ratio** says how often one step leads to the next on the way to a
support request. They let us turn the size of a service into the support it is
likely to need, so the call centre and Partner Success and Operations (PSO) can
plan before a large service joins CanadaLogin. This page uses two:

- **Calls as a share of daily users**: calls to the support line, excluding
  test calls, as a percentage of the users who sign in on a given day.
- **Share of calls escalated to PSO**: of those calls, the share the call centre
  passes to PSO for a callback.

We calculate both over four weeks at a time, from the `r chart_span_label`. The
diagram starts from how often a service's users sign in, then applies each
support ratio in turn.

:::

## Row {height="auto"}

::: {.card title="`r glue('What {monthly_users_label} monthly active users mean for support, per week')`"}

```{r ratios-diagram}
# HTML rather than a figure: real text, sized with the page, that wraps to a
# column on a narrow screen. Styled in _theme.scss.
ratio_box <- function(value, unit, range = NULL, given = FALSE) {
  htmltools::div(
    class = paste("ratio-box", if (given) "ratio-box-given"),
    htmltools::div(class = "ratio-value", value),
    htmltools::div(class = "ratio-unit", unit),
    if (!is.null(range)) htmltools::div(class = "ratio-range", range)
  )
}

ratio_arrow <- function(ratio, what, range) {
  htmltools::div(
    class = "ratio-arrow",
    htmltools::div(class = "ratio-step", ratio),
    htmltools::div(class = "ratio-what", what),
    htmltools::div(class = "ratio-line", `aria-hidden` = "true"),
    htmltools::div(class = "ratio-range", range)
  )
}

stage_range <- function(stage, unit) fmt_range(stage, \(x) fmt_rounded(x, unit))

htmltools::div(
  class = "ratio-diagram",
  htmltools::p(
    class = "ratio-legend",
    "Each box: the median week, with the middle half of simulated weeks below",
    "it. Each arrow: the median ratio, with the middle half of its values below it."
  ),
  htmltools::div(
    class = "ratio-flow",
    # The starting point is a given, not an estimate
    ratio_box(monthly_users_label, "monthly active users", given = TRUE),
    ratio_arrow(
      glue("× {pct1(step$daily_share$median)}"),
      "sign in on a typical day",
      fmt_range(step$daily_share, pct1)
    ),
    ratio_box(fmt_rounded(stage$daily_users$median, 100), "daily users",
              stage_range(stage$daily_users, 100)),
    ratio_arrow(
      glue("× 7 days × {calls_pct(step$calls_per_100$median)}"),
      "calls, as a share of daily users",
      fmt_range(step$calls_per_100, calls_pct)
    ),
    ratio_box(fmt_rounded(stage$calls$median, 10), "calls a week",
              stage_range(stage$calls, 10)),
    ratio_arrow(
      glue("× {pct1(step$escalation_rate$median)}"),
      "escalated to PSO",
      fmt_range(step$escalation_rate, pct1)
    ),
    ratio_box(fmt_rounded(stage$escalations$median, 1), "escalations a week",
              stage_range(stage$escalations, 1))
  )
)
```

::: {.figure-note}
Each box multiplies the one before it by a support ratio, calculated below.
**Sign in on a typical day** is the
[daily share of monthly users](https://cds-snc.github.io/canadalogin-metrics-cookbook/cookbook/ibm_verify/daily-share-of-monthly-users.html)
of `r n_distinct(daily_share$application_name)` public applications, with small
applications left out. This math assumes new services behave like a median
service, but a new service may not behave like any of these!
:::

:::

## Row {height="500px"}

::: {.card title="`r glue('Calls as a share of daily users ({chart_span_label})')`"}

```{r ratio-call-rate-chart}
#| fig-width: 5.4
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Calls as a share of daily users over the last three months: one grey dot per
#|   reported week, a green line through the rate over each four-week stretch,
#|   and a shaded band and dashed line marking the middle half and median of
#|   those four-week rates, labelled as in the diagram.

ratio_chart(
  drawn,
  weekly = rename(weekly_rate, window_start = week, window_end = week_end),
  y = "calls_per_100", ratio = step$calls_per_100,
  fmt = calls_pct,
  y_title = "Calls, share of daily users",
  y_labels = label_percent(accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1)
)
```

::: {.figure-note}
This counts calls, not callers: one person can call more than once, and a
caller may not have signed in that day. Elsewhere we publish this as calls
per 100 daily active users, so 0.5% here is 0.5 calls per 100.
:::

:::

::: {.card title="`r glue('Share of calls escalated to PSO ({chart_span_label})')`"}

```{r ratio-escalation-chart}
#| fig-width: 5.4
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Share of calls escalated to PSO over the last three months: one grey dot
#|   per reported week, a green line through the share over each four-week
#|   stretch, and a shaded band and dashed line marking the middle half and
#|   median of those four-week shares, labelled as in the diagram.

ratio_chart(
  drawn, weekly = weekly_escalation, y = "escalation_rate",
  ratio = step$escalation_rate, fmt = pct1,
  y_title = "Calls escalated",
  y_labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)
)
```

::: {.figure-note}
Out of calls with a topic recorded. One call can move a four-week stretch by a
percentage point. Across the stretches shown,
`r drawn_pooled$escalations` of `r comma(drawn_pooled$calls)` calls were escalated.
:::
